_request.system:
You classify a single ERP requirement into exactly one of four delivery tiers, using only the SAP standard-process knowledge entries provided to you.

  Fit           The delivered standard already does this once baseline org structures exist.
  Configuration The delivered logic does this, driven by values maintained in customizing                 (thresholds, code lists, org units, number ranges, determination rules). No code.
  Enhancement   The standard process still drives the flow, but a delivered object must carry an                 extra custom field, or extra logic must run at a published extension point.
  Development   The standard provides no object, no process, and no extension point covering the                 request; a new program, interface, or persistence must be built and maintained.

Method:
- Reason from the knowledge entries' stated boundaries: what the standard covers, what is a   configuration point, and what is stated to be beyond the standard.
- Do NOT classify from surface features. "It mentions an external system" is not a reason.   The reason must be that the standard provides no object, process, or extension point for it,   and that the transport, mapping, scheduling, and error handling are project deliverables.
- A requirement to make an already-delivered field required is field-status configuration.   A requirement to enforce entry in a field the delivered object does not have, or to gate a   process on a condition the standard data model does not carry, is an enhancement.
- In rationale, cite the specific entry IDs whose boundary decided the call, and say what that   boundary is. Cite only entries you were given.
- Set confidence below 0.7 when the entries conflict or none of them squarely covers the request.
_request.user:
Requirement (master_data): Clean country data to use standardized ISO codes, replacing inconsistent values like 'DE', 'Germany', 'Deutschland', and lower-case variations.

Verbatim from the workshop: "the compliance analyst said countries need to be cleaned into normal ISO-style codes because the old extract has DE, Germany, Deutschland, and sometimes just lower-case values."

Knowledge entries retrieved for this requirement:

### KB-MD-003 — Country, region, currency, and unit code lists [master_data]
Standard process: The system ships check tables for countries, regions, currencies, and units of measure, and the delivered country key is a short code aligned with the international standard rather than a country name. Every field that stores a country expects that short code, and the check table rejects anything else. Where an inbound source represents the same country in several ways, the reconciliation between the external representation and the internal key is maintained as conversion content: the system provides tables that map an external representation to the internal key per external system or per format. Nothing about this requires code; it requires that the mapping be maintained before the data is loaded.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Delivered check tables for country keys, regions, currencies, and units of measure.; Conversion tables that map external representations of a code to the internal key.; Validation against the check table on entry and on load.; ISO code fields alongside internal keys for currencies and units.
Common configuration points: Country keys and their properties, including the address and tax layout per country.; External-to-internal conversion entries per external system or format.; Unit of measure definitions and their ISO code assignments.; Currency keys and decimal place settings.
Typically beyond the standard: Guessing the intended code from free text at load time using fuzzy logic.; Maintaining the mapping in an application outside the ERP system and reading it at runtime.

### KB-MD-002 — Number ranges and groupings for master data [master_data]
Standard process: Master data objects draw their keys from number range intervals. An interval is either internal, meaning the system assigns the next number, or external, meaning the user or a loading program supplies the key. Intervals are assigned to a grouping or type, so different categories of the same object can be numbered separately. When a new legal entity is stood up, giving it its own intervals so that its records do not collide with those of the parent is a matter of defining intervals and assigning them to the relevant groupings. This is customizing content and needs no code.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Internal and external number assignment per object.; Multiple intervals per object, assigned by grouping, account group, or type.; Buffering and gap behaviour for high-volume assignment.
Common configuration points: Number range object intervals, including from-number, to-number, and external flag.; Assignment of intervals to business partner groupings, material types, and document types.; Separate intervals per company code or per organizational unit where the object supports it.
Typically beyond the standard: Key formats that encode business meaning the number range object cannot express.; Renumbering existing records while preserving references, which is a migration build.

### KB-R2R-002 — Financial organizational structures and the chart of accounts [R2R]
Standard process: A company code is the legal entity for which a balance sheet and profit and loss statement are produced. It is assigned an operating chart of accounts, a fiscal year variant, and a posting period variant. General ledger accounts exist at chart of accounts level and are extended to each company code that uses them. Standing up a new legal entity therefore means creating the company code, deciding whether it shares or gets its own chart of accounts, extending or creating the accounts, and setting up the fiscal year and posting period variants. These are customizing activities and master data maintenance; they do not involve code.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Company codes with their own currency, chart of accounts, and fiscal year variant.; Operating, group, and country chart of accounts layered on the same accounts.; General ledger account master at chart of accounts and company code level.; Fiscal year variants including non-calendar years and special periods.
Common configuration points: Company code definition and global parameters.; Chart of accounts definition and account groups.; Fiscal year variant and posting period variant, and their assignment.; Retained earnings account and account determination.
Typically beyond the standard: Ledger structures that the delivered parallel ledger model cannot represent.; Deriving the company code from data held outside the ERP system.

### KB-O2C-004 — Delivery blocks, export control, and trade compliance [O2C]
Standard process: A sales order or a delivery can be blocked, and the delivered blocking reasons are customizing entries assigned per document type and per customer. Trade compliance is delivered as dedicated content that screens business partners against denied party lists, classifies products against export control regulations, and checks whether a licence exists before a delivery may be released. Where a project instead requires that a human review has taken place and that its reference number is recorded on the document before release, the delivered compliance check has nothing to read: the reference field does not exist on the delivered document, so the field must be added and the release must be gated from an extension point.
Capabilities covered by the standard: Delivery and billing blocks with configurable reasons.; Denied party screening and product classification against export regulations.; Licence determination and licence-based release of deliveries.; Blocking documents until compliance checks pass.
Common configuration points: Delivery block reasons and their effect on subsequent documents.; Which document types and delivery types are subject to compliance checks.; Legal regulations, licence types, and screening parameters.
Typically beyond the standard: Requiring a bespoke review reference on the order before delivery release is permitted.; Compliance decisions recorded in an application outside the ERP system and read at release time.

parsed.rationale: KB-MD-003 states that the system provides conversion tables mapping external representations of a country to the internal key, and that maintaining these mapping entries is a configuration activity. The requirement to replace inconsistent country values like 'DE', 'Germany', 'Deutschland' with standardized ISO codes is achieved by populating these conversion entries. No code is needed, as the mapping is maintained before data is loaded.
